entries.finding: A 2026 systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of 22 randomized trials found Ashwagandha supplementation was associated with improvements in stress, depression, and anxiety outcomes, while authors emphasized heterogeneity and need for higher-quality trials.
The 2026 meta-analysis reported a significant pooled stress effect, but variation in formulations and study designs means the result should not be treated as preparation-independent.

The 2026 pooled analysis found a significant reduction in anxiety measures with Ashwagandha versus control, while noting that further well-designed trials are needed before firm clinical recommendations.

The 2026 meta-analysis found a significant pooled improvement in depression measures, but characterized Ashwagandha as promising rather than established treatment and highlighted remaining heterogeneity.

A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of 20 randomized studies involving 1,249 participants found Ashwagandha improved memory performance versus control; this evidence is distinct from evidence for treating a cognitive disorder.
The 2026 cognitive-function meta-analysis found a significant improvement in attention and processing speed with Ashwagandha supplementation.
The same 2026 meta-analysis found no significant effect of Ashwagandha on body weight or body-fat percentage, providing counterevidence to generalized weight-loss claims.
A 2026 GRADE-assessed meta-analysis of 34 randomized trials found saffron significantly reduced Beck Depression Inventory scores versus control, although heterogeneity was high.
The same 2026 synthesis found a significant reduction in Beck Anxiety Inventory scores, while no significant benefit was observed on every clinician-rated anxiety measure.
The 2026 saffron meta-analysis found no significant pooled effect on Hamilton Depression Rating Scale scores, limiting claims that benefits are consistent across depression instruments.
No significant pooled effect was observed on the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale in the 2026 saffron synthesis, providing an important null finding alongside positive self-report measures.
The 2026 review rated certainty of evidence for principal saffron mental-health findings as moderate under GRADE, despite substantial heterogeneity in several pooled outcomes.
